title: A performance refactor of AdminPermission.projects split one combined Q filter into chained .filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) calls, so read-only team members get admin rights on any project that also belongs to some admin team.

findings.explanation: The code uses Django ORM filter methods with keyword arguments and Q objects. All filtering is done through Django's parameterized query interface (filter(), exclude()) with hardcoded field names and enum-like constants (ADMIN_ACCESS, READ_ONLY_ACCESS). No raw SQL or string concatenation is present. User input is not directly interpolated into queries.

The logic change modifies how projects are filtered based on admin/member flags. The new logic has an 'else' branch that explicitly permits all team access levels when both `admin` and `member` are True. This represents a potential authorization bypass: when both flags are true, the access level filter is completely skipped, potentially allowing users to access projects they shouldn't. The comment acknowledges this behavior but it may not be intentional. The original code used OR logic (filter |= Q(...)) which would have included both conditions, while the new code skips filtering entirely when both are true.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify the intended behavior when both admin and member are True. If the intent is to include both access levels, use explicit OR logic: `projects_from_teams = projects_from_teams.filter(Q(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) | Q(teams__access=READ_ONLY_ACCESS))` instead of skipping the filter entirely with `pass`.
